finding.title: Resolve profileId live, not by snapshot, when wiring OutboxSyncWriteFacade/LocalDataUploadService/PointsBalanceDao.syncSink in syncOrchestratorProvider
finding.rule: sync push/pull invariant (docs/sync-conflict-resolution.md) / Nygard-lens: stale capture
finding.why: syncOrchestratorProvider is a keepAlive singleton that (by explicit design, per its own comments and resolveProfileIdProvider's doc) survives a profile switch without rebuilding, reacting only via `ref.listen(activeProfileIdProvider, ...)` to restart listeners. But `profileId` at line 79 is a one-time ref.read snapshot baked into OutboxSyncWriteFacade/LocalDataUploadService and into pointsBalanceDao.syncSink — not the lazy `resolveProfileId` the same function already builds at line 68 for the orchestrator's own calls. OutboxSyncWriteFacade._enqueue (features/sync/data/outbox_sync_write_facade.dart) stamps every outbox row's `profileId` column from this captured field for every entity kind it handles except learner-profile-delete (bookmarks, settings, goals, learning order, curriculum tracks, notification/gamification/UI-preference snapshots, streak events, study-day configs, and — via PointsBalanceDao._pushRedemption calling sink.enqueueRewardRedemption — reward redemptions). OutboxProcessor._doDrain only sweeps the currently-active profileId plus account-level 0 (confirmed in outbox_processor.dart and explicitly documented for the analogous deleteLearnerProfile case: 'the drain only sweeps the ACTIVE profile + 0... orphans the row'). So after a household profile switch (Bug #1/R1 already proves this happens mid-session without an orchestrator rebuild), every write of the affected kinds for the newly-active profile gets tagged with the stale boot-time profileId and is never drained until — if ever — that exact stale profile becomes active again. Concretely: parent app open with childA active, orchestrator built (profileId=A); parent switches to childB; childB redeems a reward or a bookmark/goal/track change is made; the outbox row is stamped profileId=A; the orchestrator's periodic/lifecycle/connectivity drains all resolve the live profileId (=B) and never pick up the A-stamped row. That data silently never reaches Firestore / other devices.
finding.recommendation: Change OutboxSyncWriteFacade and LocalDataUploadService to take an `int Function() resolveProfileId` (reuse resolveProfileIdProvider) instead of a captured `int profileId`, reading it at each call instead of at construction. Re-wire pointsBalanceDao.syncSink and re-run reEnqueueUnsyncedLedgerRows whenever the active profile changes, not just once at orchestrator build.
acceptance_criteria: OutboxSyncWriteFacade/LocalDataUploadService read the active profile id live at write time rather than at construction time.

Regression test: build a ProviderContainer, go cloud-born with profile A active, switch activeProfileIdProvider to B, perform a write that reaches OutboxSyncWriteFacade, and assert the resulting outbox row's profileId column equals B, not A.
Existing sync_orchestrator_providers.dart comments documenting the resolver-vs-snapshot distinction (Bug #1/R1) are updated to cover this fix.
